clue.text: New insight he develops about something King wrote

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another
a thing that develops changes its shape, so these letters are reworked into another order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone gains a fresh insight into a book by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like a royal, but it is Stephen King, the horror novelist. The rearranged letters take in N to supply the second N of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King published this horror novel in 1977, later filmed by Kubrick, so it is literally a book he wrote.

clue.text: Having week away couple leave country

indicators.note: having something away means it is taken out and gone

parts.note: a couple is two
W is the abbreviation for week, and it is removed
to leave is to depart

explanation.surface: After a week's holiday, a pair abandon their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave country' reads as emigrating, but 'leave' is wordplay and 'country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a small West African nation lying between Ghana and Benin on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Discovered family members in high spirits

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters come off

parts.note: family members are relations; lose the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Relatives were found to be in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but it means uncovered: RELATIONS loses its outer R and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a state of great happiness and excitement, the same thing as being in very cheerful spirits.

clue.text: Following try Gloucester's Number Eight gets red card

indicators.note: following says one part comes after another in the line

parts.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case

indicators.note: number eight points to the eighth letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: the eighth letter of the city name

explanation.surface: A rugby report: after a try, Gloucester's number eight forward is sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby words are all decoys: 'try' is a legal hearing, 'Number Eight' is a letter position, and the red card is from a pack, not a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts are one of the two red suits in a pack of playing cards, so any heart is a red card.

clue.text: Inquisitive nature of some Filipinos in essence

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are used, a run taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the second into the third

explanation.surface: A remark on the curious national character of people from the Philippines.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across filipiNOS IN ESSence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nosy means prying into others' business, so the noun is a prying, curious disposition.

clue.text: Ruth's mother-in-law, one with complaint returning

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a moan is a complaint

explanation.surface: A grumbling mother-in-law who keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the stock comedy mother-in-law who complains; I and MOAN are reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: In the biblical Book of Ruth, Ruth stays loyal to Naomi, the mother of her dead husband.

clue.text: Tooth grinding initially on nut

indicators.note: in an across clue, sitting on something means coming after it

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A tooth chomping on a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' seems to be the thing being chewed, but it means a devotee, as in a fitness nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth, such as a canine of a dog or the venom tooth of a snake.

clue.text: Resolute, formidable woman heading off to meet social worker

indicators.note: with its head taken off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: a madam is a bossy, imperious woman; drop the first letter
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A determined, intimidating woman sets off to see a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a council employee, but it is an ant, which lives in colonies and works.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone who refuses to be persuaded or change their mind, firmly determined.

clue.text: Religious friend, agog when converted

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eager friend after finding religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits the religious surface neatly while doing the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A god-fearing person is devout and earnestly pious, living in respect of divine authority.

clue.text: Big name releases book in haste

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so a letter is let out

parts.note: a big name is a famous person
B is the abbreviation for book, and it is removed

explanation.surface: A famous figure rushes out a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releases book' sounds like publishing, but it means CELEBRITY lets go of its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or speed of movement or action.

clue.text: Around a month to gather very fleshy fruit

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
to gather something in is to take it inside

parts.note: taken as written
AUG is the abbreviation for August
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A sweet fruit takes about a month to ripen and gather.
explanation.walkthrough: A and AUG together turn back to GUAA, which then takes V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit with soft, juicy pink or white flesh full of small seeds.

clue.text: Club, maybe twenty pounds originally, that golfer keeps

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so this part is placed first

parts.note: a score is twenty, and in slang twenty pounds
a club is one suit of playing card

explanation.surface: A golf club, perhaps costing twenty pounds at first, that a golfer holds on to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a golf club but is the card suit. The definition is a noun phrase: the thing that a golfer keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer keeps score on a card, recording strokes taken at each hole of the round.

clue.text: Sick nan Reece visits endlessly in hospital ward

indicators.note: without its end, a word loses its final letter
sick means unwell or disordered, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word loses its final S

explanation.surface: Reece keeps visiting his ill grandmother in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Nan is British for grandmother. Only the S of 'visits' is dropped before all the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive care is the hospital unit where critically ill patients receive constant monitoring and treatment.

clue.text: Little prepared almost to eat baker's first biscuit

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside itself
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: little means short

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of a word

parts.note: first letter
prepared is ready, which loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A baker's first biscuit is barely ready to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To eat' applies to the first two pieces joined together, which swallow the B at their join. A biscuit is what Americans call a cookie.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich, crumbly Scottish biscuit made from butter, sugar and flour.

clue.text: Last object, present Spooner delivered

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words when he spoke

parts.note: to object is to mind
to present a show is to host it
swap the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: The final item, a gift handed over by the Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' and 'present' look like nouns, a thing and a gift, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindmost means furthest back or behind, as in the saying 'the devil take the hindmost'.

clue.text: Bar where innumerable stars can be seen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a well-known chocolate bar

definitions.text: where innumerable stars can be seen?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the band of our galaxy across the night sky

explanation.surface: A pub or nightclub where celebrities gather in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a drinking spot full of celebrities; it is a confectionery bar, and the stars are real ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The galaxy appears as a pale band crossing the night sky made of countless distant suns.

clue.text: More suitable person installing heating system?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: comparative of an adjective meaning appropriate
second meaning: a tradesperson who installs equipment

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the heating system is just one example of what such a tradesperson might install.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of fit, meaning apt, and a noun for a mechanic who assembles and installs.

clue.text: Fail to net large fish

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it inside a mesh

parts.note: a business that fails founders
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An angler misses landing a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail' and the definition could both seem to be FLOUNDER itself, but the failing word is FOUNDER, which takes L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is a flatfish found in coastal waters, related to plaice and sole.

clue.text: Unnerve Republican, withdrawing billion from campaign

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: withdrawing something from a place means taking it out

parts.note: a military campaign is a battle
B is the abbreviation for billion, and it is removed

explanation.surface: A Republican pulls a billion dollars out of an election campaign, shaking everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as political funding; 'campaign' is a military one, BATTLE, which loses B.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to make them nervous or lose their composure, to fluster them.

clue.text: Element defending Greek character's language

indicators.note: a defender stands around what it protects, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: tin is a chemical element
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Some force protecting the language of a Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece, but it is a letter of the alphabet; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibetan is the language spoken in Tibet, written in its own script and related to Burmese.

clue.text: Make light of not working after operation

indicators.note: after says one part follows the other in the line

parts.note: in operation or in play, as of a machine part's freedom of movement
a computer system that is not working is down

explanation.surface: Someone downplays being off work after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation' suggests surgery but here it means action or activity, as when forces come into play.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to minimise its importance, treating it as less serious than it is.

clue.text: Make mistake boarding old vehicle that's occupied

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a passenger boarding goes inside the carriage

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly gets on an old bus where the seats are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupied' looks like a description of a seat, but it is the military sense of seizing territory.
explanation.definitionFit: An invading army that overran a country took control of it, spreading over it and seizing it.

clue.text: Rub lousy bonce vigorously and everything'll be fine!

indicators.note: rubbing vigorously throws things about, so the letters get mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to scrub a lice-ridden head hard and all will be well.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonce is British slang for the head, and lousy here means full of lice.
explanation.definitionFit: This British catchphrase means 'and there you have it', saying a task is simple and will turn out all right.

clue.text: Extremist braggart lunatic claims is revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution is a full turn, so the letters run backwards
to claim something is to hold it as one's own, so the words hold the letters

parts.note: the run straddles the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A boastful madman calls himself a revolutionary extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' fits the extremist picture but signals reading the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, especially in politics, a hardline zealot.

clue.text: Polish lesson

definitions.meaning: first meaning: refinement, elegance of style
second meaning: a period of teaching at school

explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes it look like a lesson in the Polish language; it is polish as in refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stylish sophistication and a scheduled session of instruction.

clue.text: Join outspoken nincompoop

indicators.note: spoken out means said out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up a mouthy idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The K is silent, so the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to unite or bind together, as broken bones knit or a team knits together.

clue.text: Removed from court, outwardly enraged by additional charge

indicators.note: by means beside, so the parts sit next to one another

parts.note: an extra is an additional charge on a bill
CT is the abbreviation for court

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone ejected from a courtroom, visibly furious at a surcharge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed from court' looks like the whole definition, but 'from' is only the link; the wordplay begins at 'court'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull or take it out, as a dentist removes a tooth.

clue.text: Part of airport, area for expansion finally

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
pro is Latin for in favour of

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A section of an airport set aside for future growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The short word 'for' looks like a connector, but it supplies PRO, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport the apron is the paved area where aircraft park, load and refuel.

clue.text: Fully cooked, it's a brownish colour reportedly

indicators.note: reported things are passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts, not spelling

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown

explanation.surface: Something cooked through has turned a brown shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning fits the cooking picture, but the colour only supplies a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is done has been cooked for long enough and is ready to eat.

clue.text: Untouchable actors abroad hosting small party in Africa

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one piece holds another
abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters are spread about

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for small
the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Untouchable actors working overseas throw a little party in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' reads as overseas, but it signals the rearrangement; S and ANC go together inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is too sacred or important to be interfered with or criticised.
